covered_actors: Large developers — nongovernmental persons or entities that have trained at least one frontier model (trained using >10^26 computational operations with compute cost >$100M, or produced via knowledge distillation from such a frontier model) costing >$5M in compute and have spent >$100M in aggregate compute costs training frontier models, including transferees receiving full intellectual property rights (excluding accredited colleges and universities engaging in academic research) (§ 1420(6), (9))
Prospective large developers setting out to train a frontier model that upon completion would qualify them as a large developer (pre-training protocol and DHSES filing duties under § 1421(7))

Contractors, subcontractors, corporate officers, and unpaid advisors involved in assessing, managing, or addressing critical-harm risks from frontier models, as well as covered employees entitled to anti-retaliation whistleblower protections (§ 1422)
Territorial scope: Frontier models developed, deployed, or operating in whole or in part in New York State (§ 1425)
prohibited_practices: Deploying a frontier model if doing so would create an unreasonable risk of critical harm (death or serious injury of 100+ people or >=$1 billion in monetary/property damages caused or materially enabled via CBRN weapons or autonomous/limited-human-intervention serious penal-law crimes) (§ 1421(2), § 1420(7))
Knowingly making false or materially misleading statements or omissions in or regarding safety and security protocols, audit reports, or incident disclosures produced under Article 44-B (§ 1421(6))

Preventing an employee (including contractors, subcontractors, corporate officers, and unpaid critical-harm risk advisors) from disclosing, or retaliating against them for disclosing or threatening to disclose, reasonable-cause concerns of unreasonable or substantial risk of critical harm to the large developer or the Attorney General (§ 1422(1))

Using contractual waivers or liability-shifting terms (including contracts of adhesion) to waive, preclude, burden, or shift liability for Article 44-B violations (void as a matter of public policy under § 1423(2)(a))

enforcement_authorities: New York Attorney General (civil enforcement actions for civil penalties up to $10M/$30M, employee anti-retaliation penalties, injunctive/declaratory relief, and access to unredacted safety protocols, audit reports, and safety incident disclosures)

New York State Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Services (DHSES) (recipient of redacted safety and security protocols, annual third-party audit reports, and 72-hour critical safety incident disclosures, with authority to request unredacted protocols/reports and share incident disclosures with the Attorney General)

New York courts (temporary or preliminary injunctive relief for whistleblowing employees under § 1422(2); piercing corporate formalities and imposing joint and several liability on affiliated entities purposely structured to evade liability under § 1423(2)(b))
compliance_deadlines: 2026-03-19 (90th day after becoming law): Effective date of Article 44-B (§ 3)

Prior to deploying a frontier model (and prior to training for prospective large developers under § 1421(7)): Implement written safety and security protocol, publish redacted copy, and transmit to DHSES (§ 1421(1), (7))
Within 72 hours of learning of a safety incident (or facts establishing reasonable belief): Disclose safety incident to DHSES (§ 1421(5))

On effective date or within 90 days of first qualifying as a large developer (and annually thereafter): Retain independent third-party auditor (§ 1421(4)(a)), conduct annual protocol review (§ 1421(3)), and inform/post conspicuous whistleblower rights notice for employees (§ 1422(3))

Duration of frontier model deployment plus 5 years: Retain unredacted safety and security protocol, update records, replicable test/evaluation records, and unredacted third-party audit reports (§ 1421(1)(b), (1)(d), (4)(d))
penalties_summary: The New York Attorney General may seek civil penalties up to $10 million for a first violation of § 1421 and up to $30 million for any subsequent violation, up to $10,000 per retaliated employee under § 1422 (awarded directly to the retaliated employee), and injunctive or declaratory relief (§ 1423(1)). Retaliated employees may also independently petition a court for temporary or preliminary injunctive relief (§ 1422(2)). Contractual liability waivers or risk-shifting clauses (including contracts of adhesion) are void as contrary to public policy, and courts must disregard corporate formalities and impose joint and several liability on affiliated entities deliberately structured to avoid or frustrate recovery (§ 1423(2)).
implementation_notes: New York S6953A adds Article 44-B (General Business Law §§ 1420–1426) governing large developers of frontier AI models (>10^26 computational operations and >$100M compute cost, plus knowledge-distilled derivatives) developed, deployed, or operating in whole or in part in New York State. Enforces pre-deployment (and pre-training for prospective large developers) written safety and security protocols covering catastrophic-risk capability evaluation and cybersecurity against sophisticated actors, a prohibition on deploying models posing unreasonable risk of critical harm, mandatory annual independent third-party compliance audits, 72-hour critical safety incident reporting to DHSES, 5-year post-deployment retention of unredacted protocols and replicable test logs, and comprehensive employee/contractor whistleblower protections. Exempts accredited colleges and universities conducting academic research.
